evals.prompt: Need a read on the Caldwell Nutrition account before my manager's pipeline review Thursday. It's a $140K ACV deal, they're about 2,400 employees, we're in evaluation. My main contact is Renata Vogel, Sr. Manager of Supply Planning - she replies within about ten minutes every time, has joined all five of our calls, and told me on call 3 'I'm the decision maker on this, don't worry about anyone else.' Also on the thread: Tomas Iriarte, VP Finance (cc'd twice, never spoken), and Aiko Brennan, a supply planning analyst who's been on two calls and loves the product. I haven't asked Renata for anything yet. Our platform stores their supplier contact records. Who's my champion and who actually signs off?
evals.expected_output: A stakeholder map that grades Renata's responsiveness as cheap behaviour rather than champion proof, caps the VP Finance economic-buyer guess at title-level confidence, flags the economic buyer as unverified with a surfacing action, sets the next ask at the bottom rung of the ladder, and hypothesises a security reviewer nobody has met.
expectations: Renata's fast replies and meeting attendance are graded as Tier 2 low-cost behaviour, not as champion evidence.
Renata's 'I'm the decision maker' statement is graded as a Tier 3 stated claim and is not treated as proof.
Renata is not assigned Champion at High confidence; she is held at Medium or lower, or labelled untested, coach, or champion-candidate.
The economic-buyer hypothesis for Tomas Iriarte rests on title only, is labelled Tier 4, and is capped at Low confidence.
The output states that at roughly 2,400 employees a VP-level title often sits two levels away from the budget, weakening title inference.
The economic buyer is either explicitly flagged unknown or named only as a Low-confidence hypothesis, with a named surfacing action attached.
At least one role-identifying question is proposed, such as who approved the last similar purchase, who holds the budget and could redirect it, or who could say no when everyone else says yes.
The next ask on the champion ladder is rung 1 - share internal evaluation criteria, competing vendors, or budget - justified by Renata being untested.
Because the product stores supplier contact records, a security or data-handling reviewer is hypothesised even though no such person has appeared.
At least one blocker hypothesis names a function that has not been on any call.
Aiko Brennan is classified as a user or cheerleader rather than as an influencer with organisational pull.
The engaged-contact count is compared against a segment benchmark and a refresh trigger is stated.

evals.prompt: We're bidding on a formal RFP from the Alderbrook Regional Transit Authority - public agency, five-year contract, they published the requirements doc and everything routes through their procurement office. Evaluation stage, responses due in six weeks. My contact is Dev Okonkwo, Deputy Director of Operations; he ran the discovery workshop and has answered every email within a day. Their CFO, Marisol Paz, signs anything over $250K. Who's my champion and what do I ask Dev for next to lock this up?
evals.expected_output: A map that removes the criteria-and-competitors ask entirely because of the public RFP, sets the next ask at a surviving rung, separates the signatory from the economic buyer, and works the blocker set in efficiency order.
expectations: Asking Dev to share internal evaluation criteria, competing bidders, or the budget is deleted from the plan, not merely deprioritised.
The deletion reason names the formal RFP or public procurement context and the risk that requesting competing-bid information can disqualify the bid.
The recommended next ask is a rung that survives the deletion - a forwardable rep-written summary, or an introduction to the economic buyer - and it is named as a rung.
The co-built business case is not deleted for stage reasons, because the deal is at evaluation rather than discovery.
The output does not recommend asking Dev who else is bidding or what the internal scoring criteria are.
Dev's responsiveness and workshop facilitation are graded no higher than Tier 2 in the absence of a capital-costing ask.
Marisol Paz is classified as signatory or budget holder rather than as the confirmed economic buyer.
The 'power to say yes when others say no, and no when others say yes' test is named as what decides the economic buyer.
Procurement appears as a mapped function, with the note that engaging it early is near-zero effort only if done before the paper stage.
Legal appears in the blocker set with a pre-emptive standard-terms play.
At least one blocker hypothesis covers a function not yet on any call.
A refresh trigger is stated.

evals.prompt: Stuck on the Peregrine Dental Group deal, $95K, proposal stage, closes end of quarter. Everything runs through Hollis Marchetti, their Director of Clinical Ops. She's great - takes every call, gave me their rollout timeline. Twice now I've asked her to set up 20 minutes with their CFO, Warren Amadi, and both times she said 'let me handle him, he trusts my recommendation.' She is genuinely the only person at that account I have a relationship with. I found Warren on LinkedIn and I'm thinking of just messaging him directly with a short note. Thoughts, and can you map this out?
evals.expected_output: A map that downgrades Hollis on two deferrals, refuses the LinkedIn bypass and deletes it because the deal is single-threaded, runs the deferral readings in their ranked order starting with the value-exchange one-pager, and flags the coverage gap.
expectations: Hollis is downgraded from champion to coach, or explicitly withheld from champion status, on the basis of two deferrals of a capital-costing ask.
Messaging Warren directly around Hollis is rejected, not merely cautioned against.
The rejection states that going around the champion can convert her into a detractor.
The bypass is deleted specifically because the deal is single-threaded, rather than kept as a fallback if the countermoves fail.
The readings of a deferred economic-buyer introduction are applied or listed, each paired with its countermove.
The first countermove run is the value exchange: a short economic-buyer-ready business case Hollis can present herself and look good doing it.
The ordering logic behind the countermoves is stated explicitly - access bought per rep hour and per unit of the contact's capital - rather than left implicit in the order they appear.
A give-to-get is offered as a softener: something Hollis wants, traded for the introduction, stated as a condition up front.
Single-threading is flagged as a coverage gap, with a named function to expand into.
The deal being over $50K and single-threaded is called structurally behind.
Warren is not recorded as a confirmed economic buyer; his assignment carries its evidence tier and confidence.
Champion risk is answered on all three points - redundancy candidate, executive sponsor, job-change detection - with any absent one marked as a gap.

evals.prompt: Mapping blockers on Tallgrass Freight Systems - $110K, mid-market, evaluation. Our product optimises trailer routing off their shipment manifests; no personal data, no consumer records, and they're not in a regulated industry. On the last call their CTO, Idris Vantol, said 'we'll need to run this through IT' and asked three questions about how we'd integrate with their TMS. My champion Simone Auer offered to set up a two-week proof of concept with their integration team, which sounds like a fast way to prove value. Their general counsel apparently reviews every vendor MSA. Give me the blocker map and tell me what order to work them in.
evals.expected_output: A blocker map ordered by veto risk removed per unit of work, with the compliance row deleted for this buyer, the proof of concept held unless a promoting condition fires, and effort given in orders of magnitude.
expectations: The blocker plays are ordered by efficiency - veto risk removed per unit of work - and that ordering is stated out loud rather than implied by row order.
Legal ranks first, with the pre-emptive play of sending standard terms before they are requested, at near-zero effort.
The compliance and privacy row is deleted for this deal, with the reason that the buyer is unregulated and the product touches no personal data.
The deleted compliance row is removed from the plan rather than carried at the bottom of the table.
The proof of concept is held rather than adopted as the next step, and the output says the efficiency order is what starves it.

A promoting condition for the proof of concept is stated: either the technical reviewer holds the real veto and has raised an integration objection the documents cannot answer, or the differentiation is only visible inside the buyer's own environment.
The output does not adopt the two-week proof of concept as the default next step merely because the champion proposed it.
Idris Vantol's integration questions are treated as a blocker signal rather than as engagement or support.
The output distinguishes the senior technical executive from whoever runs the actual technical review, noting the reviewer can hold informal veto.
Effort is expressed in orders of magnitude - near-zero, an hour, a week, a quarter - and never as a currency amount.
At least one blocker hypothesis names a function that has not appeared on any call.
Blockers are not ordered by the seniority of the person who would object.

evals.prompt: We sell residential solar. Booked a consult at a house in Fairhaven - Jodi Streit called us in, she's read everything, took the full 90-minute site walk and asked about panel degradation curves. Her husband Petar sat in for twenty minutes and said 'it's a lot of money for a roof that's eight years old.' Jodi mentioned her father helps them with big financial decisions and 'will have opinions.' System is about $34K before incentives and they'd finance it. Their 19-year-old still lives at home. I'm sending the proposal Friday - how do I read this household?
evals.expected_output: A household map using decision-making-unit roles, with the B2B-only blocker functions deleted, the father mapped as an absent hypothesis, a capital-costing ask for Jodi before Friday, and the same evidence tiers and confidence rules applied unchanged.
expectations: The household is mapped with decision-making-unit vocabulary: initiator, influencer, decider, buyer, user, gatekeeper.
Jodi is identified as the champion or initiator, and the output names what would prove it.
Petar is treated as a potential detractor or blocker rather than as a neutral participant.
The decider role is mapped onto the economic-buyer slot, and the output says whether the decider is confirmed or unknown.
Procurement, legal, security and compliance rows are deleted for this household rather than given invented household equivalents.
The job-change-detection row is dropped, and champion risk is restated as what happens if the enthusiastic partner cools before the decider engages.
The economic, political and incumbent-loyalist blockers are kept, each with a household reading.
Doing nothing, or keeping the current arrangement, is named as a live competitor.
A capital-costing ask is proposed that costs Jodi real effort, with a deadline before Friday's proposal.
The evidence tiers are applied unchanged: the 90-minute site walk and the degradation question are graded, and confidence follows the same rules as a B2B map.
The output states explicitly that this is the high-consideration household adaptation rather than leaving the transfer implicit.
The father is mapped despite never having been present, as a hypothesis rather than as an observation.

evals.prompt: Quick sanity check on Brightmoor Analytics - $180K deal, mid-market, we're at proposal. I've got nine named contacts in the CRM and I've emailed all nine at least once, so we're well past the 4-7 benchmark my manager quotes. Realistically only Kenji Haruna, their Head of Revenue Ops, actually replies; two others replied once in March and nothing since. My manager wants me at fifteen contacts before the forecast call. Am I covered, and how many more should I add?
evals.expected_output: A coverage assessment that counts real relationships rather than contacted names, calls the deal single-threaded, refuses the push to fifteen, cites the falling-consensus counter-current, and names specific unmapped roles worth adding.
expectations: Coverage is counted in real relationships rather than named contacts or email addresses, and the real-relationship count here is one.
The deal is flagged single-threaded despite nine contacted names.
The benchmark applied is the $50K-$250K band of roughly ten engaged contacts, not the 4-7 mid-market figure the user quoted.
Benchmarks are described as directional and correlational rather than as a quota or a target.
Pushing to fifteen contacts in order to hit a number is rejected.
The output cites the counter-current that purchase likelihood falls as the buying group grows - roughly 81% with one decision maker, 55% with two, the mid-30s at six.
Any multithreading win-rate lift quoted is labelled vendor-data and correlational, never causal.
Contacts are recommended only to cover named unmapped roles, and at least two such roles are named.
The deal being over $50K and single-threaded is called structurally behind.
Kenji's evidence carries a tier and his role assignment carries a confidence level.
Champion risk is answered, including whether a redundancy candidate exists.
A refresh trigger is stated.

evals.prompt: Building the stakeholder picture for Vantour Systems, $70K, evaluation stage. Two things I keep seeing quoted that I want to build around: that 40% of so-called champions fail the champion test, and that Gartner found B2B buyers consume 17 pieces of content before they decide. My contact Adaeze Nwankwo, Head of Customer Support, forwarded my one-pager to her director last week, same day I sent it. Nobody above her has spoken to us. Map it out and tell me what those numbers mean for how hard I push.
evals.expected_output: A map that refuses to build on the folklore figure, corrects the misattributed Gartner statistic and supplies the real committee figure, grades the same-day forward as a passed rung, and climbs exactly one rung from there.
expectations: The 40% champion-failure figure is labelled practitioner folklore with no traceable methodology and is not used as the basis for any recommendation.
The '17 pieces of content' claim is identified as a misattribution of Gartner's research.
The correct reading is supplied: Gartner's 17 is the share of buying time buyers spend meeting all potential suppliers combined, roughly 17%.
Gartner's actual committee figure is supplied instead - a median buying group of six to ten decision makers.
Adaeze forwarding the one-pager the same day is graded as a passed rung with follow-through inside its stated timeframe.
The forward is graded as Tier 1, and the output notes it proves willingness rather than standing.
The next ask is an introduction to the economic buyer or an executive sponsor, named as a rung.
The already-passed forwardable-summary rung is not repeated, and the output states that a second cheap ask buys no new evidence.
The largest ask - co-building and presenting the business case - is not selected as the next step.
The economic buyer is flagged unknown with a named surfacing action, since nobody above Adaeze has engaged.
Every vendor-sourced statistic appearing on the map is labelled correlational.
At least one blocker hypothesis names a function not yet on any call.

evals.prompt: Early days on Hartsfield Bioworks - we're in discovery, maybe $60K, no proposal yet and no committee formed. Three weeks ago Priyanka Deol, their Lab Operations Manager, sent me their internal scoring sheet for the two vendors they're looking at, which I'm fairly sure she wasn't supposed to share. Separately, their CFO Gideon Marsh and I worked together at my last company; I can text him any time. What should I ask Priyanka for next?
evals.expected_output: A next-ask recommendation that grades the leaked scoring sheet as the bottom rung already passed, deletes the introduction rung because the CFO relationship already exists, deletes the business-case rung because the stage has no committee, and lands on the forwardable summary.
expectations: Priyanka sharing the internal scoring sheet is graded as Tier 1 evidence and identified as the criteria-share rung already passed with follow-through.
That rung is not repeated, and the output states that a passed rung buys no new evidence.
The economic-buyer introduction rung is deleted because the existing CFO relationship means the introduction is already paid for.
The co-built business case rung is deleted because the deal sits at discovery with no committee meeting to present at.
The recommended next ask is the forwardable rep-written summary or a customer reference call, named as a rung.
Deleted rungs are removed from the plan rather than parked at the bottom of the ladder.
The output says which known fact moved which rung.
A forward-commitment phrasing is proposed that secures the commitment live on a call before the summary is written or sent.
Gideon Marsh is not automatically recorded as the confirmed economic buyer, and the 'yes when others say no' test is applied to him.
The existing CFO relationship is used to re-rank the ladder rather than as a reason to bypass Priyanka.
A blocker hypothesis is produced for at least one function not yet on any call.
Priyanka's role assignment carries an evidence tier and a confidence level.

evals.prompt: Novaris Health, $220K, evaluation, and their board meets in nine days - if we're not on that agenda it slips two quarters. My contact Bethan Ortiz, Director of Care Coordination, already spent goodwill once this month getting us a security exception fast-tracked, and she told me last Tuesday 'I can't keep asking people for favours on this.' Their architecture team floated a sandbox pilot. What do I ask for and in what order?
evals.expected_output: A re-ranked ask plan where the nine-day deadline deletes the long-latency business case, the exhausted political capital deletes the sandbox pilot, and the recommendation is a near-zero same-week ask with the constraint behind each change named.
expectations: The nine-day board deadline is used to re-rank the ask ladder, and the output says so explicitly.
The co-built business case is deleted because its exec-review latency exceeds the nine days available.
The economic-buyer introduction is flagged as carrying roughly a week of calendar latency, and is either deleted or kept only with that latency stated against the deadline.
The sandbox pilot or proof of concept is deleted on the effort ceiling, because it spends both the buyer's engineering time and Bethan's capital to schedule.
The recommended ask is a near-zero, same-week one, named as a rung.
Bethan's fast-tracked security exception is graded as Tier 1 behaviour under cost.
The output states that a contact who has already spent capital once does not start back at the bottom rung.
The output names which constraint moved which rung - the deadline for one, the effort ceiling for another.
Deleted asks are removed from the plan rather than demoted to the bottom of a list.
The output does not recommend spending Bethan's remaining capital on more than one ask before the board date.
A refresh trigger tied to the board meeting is stated.

evals.prompt: Deal: Kirkholm Manufacturing, $130K, paper stage. Their VP Engineering, Anselm Roux, signs all our contracts - he's signed two other vendor agreements this year - so he's obviously the economic buyer. The budget line for tooling software sits with Delphine Kovac, Director of Platform. I also want a MEDDPICC score out of this and a full discovery question list for my next call with Delphine. Map the stakeholders.
evals.expected_output: A map that separates signatory and budget holder from the economic buyer, leaves the economic buyer unproven with a surfacing action, supplies only the role-identifying questions, and declines both the MEDDPICC score and the full discovery set by pointing at the right skills.
expectations: Anselm is classified as signatory, and the output states that a signatory may be a delegate executing the economic buyer's decision.
Anselm is not recorded as the confirmed economic buyer on the strength of having signed other vendor agreements.
Delphine is classified as budget holder, with the note that owning a budget line does not imply authority to redirect it to this purchase.
The 'power to say yes when others say no, and no when others say yes' test is applied to decide who the economic buyer is.
The economic buyer is flagged unknown, or held at no more than Low or Medium confidence, with a surfacing action attached.
At most three role-identifying questions are supplied, rather than a full discovery question set.
The request for a full discovery question list is redirected to the discovery-questions skill rather than fulfilled here.
No MEDDPICC score, letter grade, band, or acronym-based qualification verdict is produced.
The MEDDPICC request is redirected to the MEDDPICC scorecard skill by name.
At the paper stage, procurement and legal both appear on the blocker map with their plays.
Every named stakeholder carries a role, an evidence tier with the evidence itself, a confidence level, and a next action.
